assumptions.payload_model: each selected pair stages both up and down expert tensors; native model expert tensor bytes come from fallback CSV and GGUF manifest where available
assumptions.profile_scope: no prompt-specific single-prompt profile; global topN pairs are ranked by summed decode fallback time across all calibration/dev prompts
assumptions.zero_overhead_model: subtracts selected pair fallback_ms from current decode window; excludes real staging, H2D/D2H, kernel launch, indexing, and prompt/TTFT overhead, so this is an optimistic upper bound

decision.next_action: Do not implement prompt/hotset-specific sparse pair staging. Return to exact generic dataflow: remove up/down CPU fallback by using selected_experts/weights tensors in the graph or by introducing a compact per-token exact-gather GPU path, then prove coverage on calibration/dev before touching held-out.
decision.summary: Generalized sparse pair hotset is rejected as a main optimization route. The distribution is too diffuse: top2048 already needs about 17.0 GiB of up/down payload and still has a 43-layer zero-overhead min of 2.76 tok/s; top4096 needs about 34.0 GiB and still leaves quantum/fibonacci below 5 tok/s; even all 6485 observed pairs need about 53.8 GiB and Fibonacci remains below 5 under the existing full-up/down zero-overhead model.

extended_payload_curve_no_profile_files.description: Extended generalized hotset curve computed from the same calibration/dev fallback CSVs without writing large profile files for topN above 512. Held-out set is not used. This is still a zero-overhead upper bound.
